facts.label: Credit-relevant observations on source limits
facts.text: - Leverage and covenant evidence. The annual report prints the ABL tests ("The maximum Leverage Ratio is 5.25 to 1.00", a secured leverage maximum of 3.25 to 1.00 and "a minimum interest coverage ratio of 2.5x", 10-K page:72). The 2026 quarterlies state "we were in compliance with all covenants under the ABL Facility" (10-Q 2026-06-30 page:21) and that the Fifth Amendment "modifies the calculation of the leverage ratio" through June 30, 2026, but do not restate levels or the amended definition. Mechanism: the covenant EBITDA and Total Indebtedness are "each as defined in the ABL Credit Agreement", which is not supplied, and management's ratios in the releases (for example "credit agreement leverage ratio was 3.2x for the second quarter of 2026", release 2026-08-06 page:5) are attributed claims. Consequence: CP-1 can report the printed tests and management ratios as separately labelled claims but cannot recompute covenant headroom or confirm terms after June 30, 2026. - Perimeter change. The June 2026 quarter is the first to include the acquired power business, whose purchase accounting "remains preliminary" (10-Q 2026-06-30 page:13); the first quarter filing states valuations were incomplete (10-Q 2026-03-31 page:24). Mechanism: goodwill, intangibles and the opening balance sheet can still change within the measurement period, and pre-April periods contain no power results. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 must not present year-over-year growth or leverage across the April 2026 boundary as like-for-like; the pro forma table (10-Q 2026-06-30 page:15) is the only filed bridge and is not a forecast. - Capital structure change within the period. Notes due 2029 were replaced by notes due 2031 in March and April 2026 with a defeasance and a loss on extinguishment (10-Q 2026-06-30 page:21-22), and an equity offering closed in May 2026 with "aggregate net proceeds of approximately $836.1 million" (page:26). Mechanism: the December 2025 debt table and the June 2026 debt table list different instruments. Consequence: CP-1 must extract facility-level debt at each balance-sheet date separately and carry the refinancing as a flow, not as a restatement. - Off-debt claims. Purchase commitments are stated as "$2.5 billion, of which $587.9 million is expected to be settled within the next twelve months" (page:29), lease payments and a regulatory matter are disclosed (page:30, page:32). Mechanism: these sit outside the debt table, and the filing gives no estimate of penalties for the regulatory matter. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 must show them as separate claims, with the regulatory matter flagged as an unquantified contingency. - Authority split. Filed statements and notes control financial facts; the releases supply non-GAAP measures, guidance and narrative such as "Record Compression Infrastructure segment revenues". Consequence: management characterisations may be carried only as attributed claims, and a release figure that differs from a filing yields to the filing.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is adequate for a bounded credit snapshot at the June 30, 2026 balance sheet date, with metrics that must be read as adjusted-EBITDA, principal-debt measures built from filed statements and company reconciliations. On those measures leverage has stepped down since December 2024: total debt to adjusted EBITDA is 4.31x at FY2024, 3.66x at FY2025, 3.92x on LTM March 2026 (when the notes refinancing had raised principal debt before the acquisition closed and before the May equity offering) and 3.63x on LTM June 2026. Interest cover on cash interest paid is 4.14x on LTM June 2026. Secured debt is small, because only the ABL is secured, and the next maturity of size is the ABL in 2030, followed by the unsecured notes from 2031. Three features temper that picture: the acquired power business contributes earnings only from April 1, 2026, so LTM EBITDA understates a full-year perimeter against debt and equity that already include its financing; operating cash conversion weakened in the first half of 2026; and purchase commitments rose sharply while guidance implies negative free cash flow in 2026. Covenant headroom is stated by management, not recomputed. No pension, retiree, factoring or supply-chain finance obligations were located in the 10-K or June 2026 10-Q.

facts.text: - C1. LTM June 2026 construction. Revenue: 1,308,100 (FY2025, 10-K page:99) + 736,879 (H1 2026, 10-Q page:6) - 652,485 (H1 2025) = 1,392,494. Adjusted EBITDA: 715,033 (release 2026-02-25 page:13) + 406,938 (10-Q page:56) - 355,880 = 766,091. Check by four quarters: 174,702 + 184,451 + 190,092 + 216,846 = 766,091. Net income: 81,588 + 70,004 - 71,020 = 80,572; four quarters (14,197) + 24,765 + 17,860 + 52,144 = 80,572. Operating cash flow: 599,740 + 170,647 - 291,500 = 478,887; four quarters 113,378 + 194,862 + 71,182 + 99,465 = 478,887. Discretionary cash flow: 461,684 + 289,756 - 232,508 = 518,932; four quarters 116,652 + 112,524 + 126,505 + 163,251 = 518,932. Free cash flow: 229,581 + (50,534) - 117,509 = 61,538; four quarters 33,463 + 78,609 + 36,962 + (87,496) = 61,538 (H1 values from 10-Q page:57-58). - C2. LTM March 2026 adjusted EBITDA: 715,033 + 190,092 - 177,664 (Q1 2025, 10-Q 2026-03-31 page:43) = 727,461; check Q2 2025 178,216 + Q3 2025 174,702 + Q4 2025 184,451 + Q1 2026 190,092 = 727,461. Cash interest: 168,716 + 41,349 - 57,330 (10-Q 2026-03-31 page:8) = 152,735. - C3. LTM June 2026 cash interest: 168,716 + 103,535 - 87,075 = 185,176. Quarterly cash interest by subtraction: Q2 2026 = 103,535 - 41,349 = 62,186; Q2 2025 = 87,075 - 57,330 = 29,745. Revenue LTM March 2026 = 1,308,100 + 345,759 - 329,642 = 1,324,217. - C4. Leverage. FY2024: 2,625,097 / 609,550 = 4.31x; net (2,625,097 - 4,750) = 2,620,347 / 609,550 = 4.30x. FY2025: 2,614,647 / 715,033 = 3.66x; net 2,611,468 / 715,033 = 3.65x. LTM March 2026: 2,849,936 / 727,461 = 3.92x; net (2,849,936 - 94,363) = 2,755,573 / 727,461 = 3.79x. LTM June 2026: 2,780,917 / 766,091 = 3.63x; net (2,780,917 - 137,553) = 2,643,364 / 766,091 = 3.45x. Interest cover on cash interest: 609,550 / 147,144 = 4.14x; 715,033 / 168,716 = 4.24x; 727,461 / 152,735 = 4.76x; 766,091 / 185,176 = 4.14x. Cover on interest expense: FY2025 715,033 / 198,370 = 3.60x; FY2024 609,550 / 197,144 = 3.09x; LTM June 2026 interest expense 198,370 + 98,802 - 92,979 = 204,193, 766,091 / 204,193 = 3.75x. - C5. Unadjusted EBITDA and add-backs. FY2025: net income 81,588 + interest 198,370 + tax 31,884 + depreciation and amortization 276,185 = 588,027; add-backs 6,344 + 24,529 + 2,497 + 4,102 + 27,968 + 33,349 + 28,217 = 127,006; 588,027 + 127,006 = 715,033, equal to the reported figure. LTM June 2026: net income 80,572 + interest 204,193 + tax (31,884 + 23,853 - 23,969 = 31,768) + D&A (276,185 + 147,331 - 136,664 = 286,852) = 603,385; add-backs: loss on extinguishment 36,512; disposal of business 33,349; sales tax reserve 27,968; loss on sale of assets 28,217 + 4,220 - 15,817 = 16,620; equity compensation 24,529 + 14,529 - 13,269 = 25,789; transaction expenses 4,102 + 11,615 - 1,786 = 13,931; severance 2,497 + 72 - 376 = 2,193; impairment 6,344; total 162,706; 603,385 + 162,706 = 766,091 (equal to C1). Share of add-backs: 162,706 / 766,091 = 21.2%. Unadjusted leverage: 2,780,917 / 603,385 = 4.61x; net 2,643,364 / 603,385 = 4.38x. Cash taxes LTM: 5,939 + 4,299 - 5,393 = 4,845; tax expense LTM 31,768 as above. - C6. Cash conversion. Operating cash flow / adjusted EBITDA: FY2024 327,987 / 609,550 = 53.8%; FY2025 599,740 / 715,033 = 83.9%; LTM June 2026 478,887 / 766,091 = 62.5%. Adjusted EBITDA percentage LTM: 766,091 / 1,392,494 = 55.0%. Purchase of PP&E LTM: 315,472 + 318,579 - 160,171 = 473,880. Dividends LTM: 159,557 + 92,601 - 76,593 = 175,565. - C7. Liquidity. Undrawn = 2,000,000 - drawn - letters of credit. Sep 30, 2025: 2,000,000 - 521,492 - 2,400 = 1,476,108. Dec 31, 2025: 2,000,000 - 464,647 - 1,400 = 1,533,953; with cash 3,179 gives 1,537,132. Mar 31, 2026: 2,000,000 - 449,936 - 1,400 = 1,548,664. Jun 30, 2026: 2,000,000 - 380,917 - 14,600 = 1,604,483; with cash 137,553 gives 1,742,036. The December 2025, March 2026 and June 2026 results agree with the company statements of about $1.5 billion, $1.5 billion and $1.6 billion available; no statement was checked for September 2025. Purchase commitments within twelve months 587,900 / 1,742,036 = 33.7% of June 2026 liquidity (shown for scale; not used elsewhere). - C8. Covenant-related indications. Management 3.2x against 5.25x: 5.25 - 3.2 = 2.05 turns; EBITDA cushion 1 - 3.2 / 5.25 = 39.0%. Secured debt: ABL drawn 380,917 / 766,091 = 0.50x. Lease-inclusive total debt: 2,780,917 + 4,283 + 48,246 + 48,259 = 2,881,705; / 766,091 = 3.76x. Secured leverage and interest cover here use analyst definitions and are not the covenant calculations. - C9. Guidance and dividend. Low-case discretionary cash flow less high-case capital expenditure: 570,000 - 805,000 = (235,000). High-case: 600,000 - 725,000 = (125,000). Quarterly dividend: $0.49 x 101,104,031 shares = 49,541 thousand (rounded); excludes the corresponding Kodiak Services distribution on OpCo Units, paired with 224 thousand preferred shares at June 30, 2026 (10-Q page:9, page:26, page:35). - C10. Maturity table check: 2,780,917 + 4,283 = 2,785,200, equal to the printed total on page:24. Other borrowings 4,283 equals remainder-2026 1,822 plus 2027 2,461. - C11. Capital expenditure bridge, Q2 2026: growth and other capital expenditure 254,870 (release 2026-08-06 page:6) less non-cash finance lease addition 42,600 less increase in accrued capital expenditure 32,000 (10-Q page:58) = 180,270; cash purchase of PP&E for the quarter 200,209 (318,579 - 118,370 for Q1 2026, 10-Q 2026-03-31 page:8) less maintenance capital expenditure 19,947 = 180,262; the 8 difference is rounding of the 42.6 million and 32.0 million disclosed in millions. Expense block reconciliation, Q2 2026: revenue 391,120 less cost of operations (94,435 + 11,686 + 38,235 = 144,356) less depreciation and amortization 78,650 less SG&A 40,918 less loss on sale of assets 2,959 = 124,237, equal to reported income from operations. FY2025: 1,308,100 less cost of operations (373,493 + 106,432 = 479,925) less 276,185 less impairment 6,344 less SG&A 144,070 less loss on sale of assets 61,566 = 340,010, equal to reported.

facts.text: Kodiak's credit story is a contract compression operator with fixed-fee, multi-year contracts, high fleet utilisation and customers described as large upstream and midstream companies, that is in the middle of a strategic widening into distributed power. On the evidence, the compression core is stable and gaining visibility: remaining performance obligations rose sharply in the second quarter of 2026 and utilisation was 98.2%. The power build is the new variable. The acquisition closed on April 1, 2026, the acquired business has produced one quarter of results, only one customer lease is disclosed in detail, and purchase commitments rose to $2.5 billion. The financial handoff shows an equity offering, a refinanced notes stack and a largely undrawn ABL alongside this growth, which supports near-term liquidity but moves the credit from a steady-state contract business toward a capital-intensive build in which the pace of customer contracting, not demand commentary, matters. Ownership is public: the former sponsor affiliate exited in 2025, so no sponsor is documented as supporting or controlling the credit. Documented capital allocation shows both shareholder distributions and equity issuance; no priming, drop-down, non-pro-rata exchange or collateral release is documented in the pack. Governance evidence is limited to filing summaries because the proxy statement and executed financing documents are not supplied.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The transaction that matters most is the acquisition of Distributed Power Solutions, LLC, a provider of turnkey distributed and behind-the-meter power generation, by Kodiak Gas Services, LLC. The type is an acquisition of 100% of the equity interests for cash and registrant shares. Signing was on February 5, 2026 at a value of approximately $675.0 million at signing, comprising $575.0 million of cash and 2,401,278 shares valued at approximately $100.0 million on a $41.64 five-day average price, with a $37.1 million termination fee payable by the registrant in certain circumstances (10-K pages 25 and 139). Closing was April 1, 2026 on cash of $587.3 million, adjusted for additional power generation assets bought before closing, indebtedness and working capital, and 2.4 million shares with an estimated fair value of $139.0 million at the $57.90 closing price, so the fair value of consideration transferred was 726,354 thousand USD (10-Q 2026-06-30 pages 12 and 13; 10-Q 2026-03-31 page 24). The sellers are not named in the acquisition note; the registration rights agreement entered at closing names Mustang PRS, LLC and Louisiana Machinery Company, L.L.C. as holders of the registrant shares issued in the transaction (10-Q 2026-03-31 page 24); the pack does not otherwise name the sellers. The purchase price allocation is preliminary and recognises goodwill of 344,782 thousand USD, all in the Power Infrastructure reporting unit (10-Q 2026-06-30 pages 13 and 19). The pack contains no bridge between the signing and closing values, so the difference is logged as a conflict below and not reconciled. The stated rationale, which is management language, is to expand beyond contract compression into distributed power generation and enhance revenue growth through scale and complementary services (10-Q 2026-06-30 page 12). Liquidity effect and use of proceeds: the notes and equity transactions that followed are described below; the pack does not state which source funded which part of the cash consideration, and the financial handoff shows cash paid net of cash acquired of 575,965 thousand USD in the first half of 2026. The status is complete, with the allocation open for up to one year from closing.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New debt in the period. On March 20, 2026 Kodiak Services issued $1.0 billion of 5.875% senior unsecured notes due 2031, with fees of $14.3 million, and used a portion of the net proceeds to redeem all $750.0 million of its 7.25% notes due 2029 at 103.625 percent, through a defeasance on March 30, 2026 that required a $785.5 million cash outlay and produced a loss on extinguishment of 36,512 thousand USD (10-Q 2026-06-30 pages 21 to 23). The 2029 notes were redeemed April 10, 2026. On April 2, 2026 Kodiak and Kodiak Services signed the Fifth Amendment to the ABL credit agreement, which modifies the leverage ratio calculation by allowing net proceeds of the 2031 notes to be deducted from total indebtedness, in addition to the $50.0 million cash netting cap, through June 30, 2026 (page 21). In the prior year, on September 5, 2025 Kodiak Services issued $600.0 million each of 6.50% notes due 2033 and 6.75% notes due 2035, with add-ons of $170.0 million and $30.0 million on September 22, 2025, using the proceeds to repay part of the ABL, and a Fourth Amendment to the ABL reduced commitments to $2.0 billion and extended maturity to September 2030 (10-Q 2026-06-30 page 23; 10-K page 72), the amendment date not being stated in the text read. The equity side: an underwritten offering of 10.6 million shares at $71.00, with a further 1.6 million shares under the option, closed May 15, 2026 for net proceeds of approximately $836.1 million (10-Q 2026-06-30 page 26). The pack does not state a use of proceeds for that offering, and the financial handoff shows ABL drawings fell in the quarter; the link is an inference, not a documented fact. After quarter end Kodiak exercised options to buy about 43,000 horsepower of leased compression equipment for about $32.8 million in July 2026 and declared a $0.49 per share dividend on August 5, 2026 (10-Q 2026-06-30 pages 29 and 35). The financial handoff carries the resulting leverage, liquidity and maturity figures: total debt to LTM adjusted EBITDA of 3.63x, liquidity of 1,742.0 US$m, and purchase commitments of $2.5 billion. Parties, status and amounts above are Documentary Facts; the stated rationales are Management Language; the possible link between the equity offering and ABL repayment is Analyst Interpretation.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: fixed monthly fees with primary terms of one to seven years (10-K page:16), 9.0% of revenue-generating horsepower on month-to-month terms, and performance obligations of 2,643,245 thousand USD at June 30, 2026 against LTM compression revenue of 1,220,890 thousand USD (Calculation A2). Mechanic: take-or-pay-style fees convert fleet utilisation into near-term revenue regardless of volumes, and the rise in obligations extends the contracted period. Implication: supports near-term revenue visibility and debt service; the step up is unexplained, and the tail beyond 2027 was thin until the second quarter. Counter: the shorter-term tail and month-to-month contracts are the exposure if basin activity weakens. 2. Margin and cash-flow risk (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: Compression adjusted gross margin of 70.0% in the second quarter against Other Services at 11.3%, below 15.9% in the first quarter of 2026 and 24.5% a year earlier (release 2026-08-06 page:6), with receivables and working capital absorbing cash in the first half (financial handoff, cash flow quality). Mechanic: the high-margin compression stream carries the credit; Other Services margin erosion and working capital drag reduce cash conversion. Implication: credit metrics on adjusted EBITDA overstate cash earnings in 2026; the financial handoff shows operating cash flow at 62.5% of LTM adjusted EBITDA. 3. Concentration risk (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: 82.8% of compression assets in the Permian Basin and Eagle Ford (10-K page:13), four largest customers about 32% of revenue and one customer 14%, and a limited number of suppliers. Mechanic: basin activity, a single large customer's decisions and equipment lead times drive utilisation and growth timing. Implication: loss of the largest customer or a supplier disruption would have a disproportionate effect on utilisation and growth timing; no peer comparison is made. 4. Transformation and execution risk in power (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: one disclosed lease with initial term to April 1, 2028, revised power growth capital spending guidance, purchase commitments of $2.5 billion against $276.4 million at March 31, 2026 (10-Q 2026-03-31 page:34), and a one gigawatt turbine order (release 2026-08-06 page:2). Mechanic: equipment is bought before multi-year contracts are shown, so cash is committed ahead of revenue; power lease revenue was 8.4% of second quarter revenue (Calculation A3). Implication: liquidity of 1,742.0 US$m in the financial handoff must absorb a 12-month commitment of $587.9 million plus negative implied free cash flow; delays in contracting would raise leverage because EBITDA from the new assets lags the financing. Counter: management states customer discussions are advanced, a Management Language claim that is not backed by executed contracts in the pack. 5. Sponsor alignment (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: the sponsor affiliate holding fell to zero by December 2, 2025 with no proceeds to Kodiak. Mechanic: with no sponsor, distributions and acquisitions are decided by a public-company board under the covenant package; ABL-funded dividends require $100,000,000 pro forma availability. Implication: no sponsor is documented as available to provide support, and equity issuance at market is the demonstrated support route; monitoring should track distributions against free cash flow, which in 2025 were 263,525 thousand USD against company free cash flow of 229,581 thousand USD (Calculation A4). 6. Key uncertainties (Analyst Interpretation). Preliminary purchase accounting; an unquantified sanctions-related matter; unexplained allowance write-offs; and no executed financing documents. Each is a gap below.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Kodiak Gas Services is a moderately leveraged contract compression credit whose strength is contracted, high-margin revenue and ample liquidity, and whose main exposure is a power build financed ahead of contracts. Compression remaining performance obligations of USD 2,643.2 million, utilisation of 98.2% and total debt of 3.63x LTM adjusted EBITDA after an equity raise of USD 836.1 million support the credit, with liquidity of USD 1,742.0 million and no scheduled debt maturity of size before 2030. The weakest point is that growth spending outruns cash generation: purchase commitments are USD 2.5 billion, guidance implies negative 2026 free cash flow, and only one power lease is disclosed. Delivery of power contracts against that spending, and covenant headroom that cannot be recomputed here, decide the outcome.

facts.text: Kodiak's cash-generative, contracted compression fleet and equity-supported balance sheet carry the credit through a power build whose repayment capacity is not yet evidenced by contracts (Analyst Interpretation, resting on the contract, leverage and commitment rows below).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The first finding is revenue durability. Kodiak sells compression on fixed monthly fees under primary terms of one to seven years, with 9.0% of revenue-generating horsepower on month-to-month terms, and its compression remaining performance obligations were USD 2,643.2 million at June 30, 2026 against USD 1,632.9 million at March 31, 2026, with 49.9% falling in 2028 or later (Documentary Fact, from the business-context handoff). The mechanism is that fixed fees turn 98.2% utilisation into revenue largely independent of volume, so contracted obligations of 2.17 times LTM compression revenue protect near-term coverage of debt service. The implication is stronger revenue visibility than the previous quarter showed, tempered because the filings do not explain the jump and the month-to-month tail would reprice quickly in a weak basin.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The second is financial risk and leverage. Total debt was USD 2,780.9 million, or 3.63x LTM adjusted EBITDA of USD 766.1 million, and net debt was 3.45x, against 4.31x total and 4.30x net at FY2024 and 3.66x total at FY2025 (Documentary Fact for inputs, Calculated in the financial-base handoff). The mechanism is that the May equity offering of USD 836.1 million arrived in the same period as the USD 576.0 million cash acquisition and a notes refinancing, so debt rose by USD 166.3 million since December 2025 while LTM adjusted EBITDA rose by USD 51.1 million. The implication for leverage tolerance is a stepped-down but not yet clearly falling ratio; the figure overstates leverage on a full-year perimeter because EBITDA from the acquired power business before April 1, 2026 is Not calculable, and management's covenant-basis ratio of 3.2x (Management Language) cannot be recomputed.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The third is funding and liquidity. Liquidity was USD 1,742.0 million (cash of USD 137.6 million and undrawn ABL capacity of USD 1,604.5 million, an upper bound because the borrowing base is not supplied), against purchase commitments of USD 2.5 billion, of which USD 587.9 million is expected within twelve months, up from USD 276.4 million at March 31, 2026. Revised 2026 guidance implies discretionary cash flow less growth and other capital spending of negative USD 235.0 million to negative USD 125.0 million, before dividends of about USD 49.5 million a quarter. The mechanism is that the spending is discretionary in timing but contractually committed once ordered, and the ABL, which matures September 5, 2030 and is secured on essentially all assets, is the funding backstop. The implication is that refinancing risk is low through 2029 but that net leverage, on the indicative sensitivity below, ends 2026 at about 3.27x to 3.52x, roughly where it is today, unless adjusted EBITDA beats guidance or equity is raised again (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The fourth is earnings and cash quality. Add-backs were USD 162.7 million, or 21.2% of LTM adjusted EBITDA, and unadjusted leverage on the same debt would be 4.61x; operating cash flow was 62.5% of LTM adjusted EBITDA against 83.9% in FY2025, as working capital used USD 154.6 million in the first half (Documentary Fact and Calculated). The mechanism is that equity compensation, a settled sales tax reserve and refinancing and acquisition costs sit outside adjusted EBITDA while the sales tax settlement and working capital absorbed cash. The implication is that adjusted-EBITDA coverage of 4.14x on cash interest paid is a ceiling on debt-service capacity, and monitoring should use operating cash flow.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The fifth is the power transition and ownership. The acquisition closed April 1, 2026 with fair value of consideration of USD 726.4 million (signing value was about USD 675.0 million, logged as a conflict, not reconciled), goodwill of USD 344.8 million on a preliminary allocation, one disclosed lease agreement whose initial term ends April 1, 2028, and no sponsor, since EQT affiliates sold their entire stake by December 2, 2025 (Documentary Fact). The mechanism is that equipment is bought before multi-year contracts are shown, and no sponsor is documented as available to cure a shortfall. The implication is that the next two to three quarters of power contract announcements and utilisation are the main evidence that will move the credit view either way.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Contracted revenue visibility is the first: fixed-fee compression contracts, 98.2% utilisation, performance obligations of USD 2,643.2 million, and customer cost pass-throughs for fuel and taxes (Documentary Fact; business-context handoff). Margin resilience is the second: compression adjusted gross margin was 70.0% in the second quarter and adjusted EBITDA margin was 55.4% (Documentary Fact; financial-base handoff), which cushions a revenue decline. Liquidity and maturity profile is the third: USD 1,742.0 million of liquidity, no scheduled maturity of size before the ABL in 2030, and notes of USD 1,000.0 million due 2031, USD 770.0 million due 2033 and USD 630.0 million due 2035 (Documentary Fact). Balance sheet response is the fourth: Kodiak issued USD 836.1 million of equity alongside a debt-financed acquisition (Documentary Fact), which is documented equity support. Secured debt is the fifth: only the USD 380.9 million drawn on the ABL is secured, equal to 0.50x LTM adjusted EBITDA on this analysis (Analyst Interpretation, indicative only because the covenant definition of senior secured debt is not supplied).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Growth spending against cash flow is the first: commitments of USD 2.5 billion and guidance that implies negative free cash flow in 2026 (Analyst Interpretation on Documentary Fact inputs). Earnings quality is the second: add-backs of 21.2% of LTM adjusted EBITDA and weaker cash conversion of 62.5% (Documentary Fact and Calculated). Concentration is the third: 82.8% of compression assets in the Permian Basin and Eagle Ford, four customers at about 32% of revenue and one at 14%, and dependence on a limited number of suppliers (Documentary Fact). Power visibility is the fourth: one disclosed lease agreement, so most power revenue is Not disclosed in contract terms, and a power fleet utilisation of 89.6% in its first quarter (Documentary Fact; the conclusion that visibility is thin is Analyst Interpretation). Covenant opacity is the fifth: the maximum Leverage Ratio of 5.25 to 1.00 printed in the annual report is on a defined basis not supplied, and the amended calculation applied only through June 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact; headroom is Insufficient Information). Unquantified contingencies are the sixth: a sanctions-related payments matter with no estimated penalty and a sales tax liability disclosed on two bases (Documentary Fact; exposure is Insufficient Information, not an adverse conclusion).

facts.text: - D1. Debt and EBITDA change since December 2025: total debt 2,780,917 - 2,614,647 = 166,270; LTM adjusted EBITDA 766,091 - 715,033 (FY2025) = 51,058. Cash acquisition cost 575,965 (net of cash acquired). Contracted obligations to LTM compression revenue: 2,643,245 / 1,220,890 = 2.17 times (financial base and business context handoffs). - D2. Indicative year-end 2026 net leverage on management guidance (Analyst Interpretation, not a forecast). Full-year guidance: discretionary cash flow 570,000 to 600,000; growth and other capital spending 725,000 to 805,000; adjusted EBITDA 830,000 to 860,000. First half actuals: discretionary cash flow 289,756; growth and other capital spending 134,357 + 152,356 + 61,167 = 347,880. Implied second half: best case 600,000 - 289,756 = 310,244 of discretionary cash flow against 725,000 - 347,880 = 377,120 of spending, a shortfall of 66,876; worst case 570,000 - 289,756 = 280,244 against 805,000 - 347,880 = 457,120, a shortfall of 176,876. Add dividends of two quarters at 49,541 = 99,082 (per share dividend of USD 0.49 on 101,104,031 shares, constant). Net debt need: 165,958 (best) and 275,958 (worst). Net debt at June 30, 2026 is 2,643,364, so year-end net debt is 2,809,322 (best) and 2,919,322 (worst). Net leverage: best 2,809,322 / 860,000 = 3.27x; worst 2,919,322 / 830,000 = 3.52x. Gross total debt equivalents, holding cash constant: (2,780,917 + 165,958) / 860,000 = 3.43x and (2,780,917 + 275,958) / 830,000 = 3.68x. The inputs mix company non-GAAP definitions with guidance; asset sale proceeds, working capital, further equity and interest on additional borrowings are not modelled. - D3. Liquidity cover of twelve-month commitments: 587,900 / 1,742,036 = 33.7% of June 2026 liquidity (financial base handoff); liquidity less commitments 1,742,036 - 587,900 = 1,154,136.

Power customer contracts and portfolio beyond one disclosed lease not disclosed

No filing for the quarter ended September 30, 2026
No ratings, market data or peer data; context fields blank

### Credit-relevant observations on source limits
Evidence, then source-risk mechanism, then downstream consequence, for the items that bind most.

- Leverage and covenant evidence. The annual report prints the ABL tests ("The maximum Leverage Ratio is 5.25 to 1.00", a secured leverage maximum of 3.25 to 1.00 and "a minimum interest coverage ratio of 2.5x", 10-K page:72). The 2026 quarterlies state "we were in compliance with all covenants under the ABL Facility" (10-Q 2026-06-30 page:21) and that the Fifth Amendment "modifies the calculation of the leverage ratio" through June 30, 2026, but do not restate levels or the amended definition. Mechanism: the covenant EBITDA and Total Indebtedness are "each as defined in the ABL Credit Agreement", which is not supplied, and management's ratios in the releases (for example "credit agreement leverage ratio was 3.2x for the second quarter of 2026", release 2026-08-06 page:5) are attributed claims. Consequence: CP-1 can report the printed tests and management ratios as separately labelled claims but cannot recompute covenant headroom or confirm terms after June 30, 2026.

- Perimeter change. The June 2026 quarter is the first to include the acquired power business, whose purchase accounting "remains preliminary" (10-Q 2026-06-30 page:13); the first quarter filing states valuations were incomplete (10-Q 2026-03-31 page:24). Mechanism: goodwill, intangibles and the opening balance sheet can still change within the measurement period, and pre-April periods contain no power results. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 must not present year-over-year growth or leverage across the April 2026 boundary as like-for-like; the pro forma table (10-Q 2026-06-30 page:15) is the only filed bridge and is not a forecast.

- Capital structure change within the period. Notes due 2029 were replaced by notes due 2031 in March and April 2026 with a defeasance and a loss on extinguishment (10-Q 2026-06-30 page:21-22), and an equity offering closed in May 2026 with "aggregate net proceeds of approximately $836.1 million" (page:26). Mechanism: the December 2025 debt table and the June 2026 debt table list different instruments. Consequence: CP-1 must extract facility-level debt at each balance-sheet date separately and carry the refinancing as a flow, not as a restatement.

- Off-debt claims. Purchase commitments are stated as "$2.5 billion, of which $587.9 million is expected to be settled within the next twelve months" (page:29), lease payments and a regulatory matter are disclosed (page:30, page:32). Mechanism: these sit outside the debt table, and the filing gives no estimate of penalties for the regulatory matter. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 must show them as separate claims, with the regulatory matter flagged as an unquantified contingency.

- Authority split. Filed statements and notes control financial facts; the releases supply non-GAAP measures, guidance and narrative such as "Record Compression Infrastructure segment revenues". Consequence: management characterisations may be carried only as attributed claims, and a release figure that differs from a filing yields to the filing.

### Financial base view

The financial base is adequate for a bounded credit snapshot at the June 30, 2026 balance sheet date, with metrics that must be read as adjusted-EBITDA, principal-debt measures built from filed statements and company reconciliations. On those measures leverage has stepped down since December 2024: total debt to adjusted EBITDA is 4.31x at FY2024, 3.66x at FY2025, 3.92x on LTM March 2026 (when the notes refinancing had raised principal debt before the acquisition closed and before the May equity offering) and 3.63x on LTM June 2026. Interest cover on cash interest paid is 4.14x on LTM June 2026. Secured debt is small, because only the ABL is secured, and the next maturity of size is the ABL in 2030, followed by the unsecured notes from 2031. Three features temper that picture: the acquired power business contributes earnings only from April 1, 2026, so LTM EBITDA understates a full-year perimeter against debt and equity that already include its financing; operating cash conversion weakened in the first half of 2026; and purchase commitments rose sharply while guidance implies negative free cash flow in 2026. Covenant headroom is stated by management, not recomputed. No pension, retiree, factoring or supply-chain finance obligations were located in the 10-K or June 2026 10-Q.

### Consumption of the source-readiness handoff

The source-readiness handoff was opened and its limitations are applied as follows. Its differences: D1 (acquisition price, announced approximately $675.0 million versus closing fair value 726,354) is carried; this module uses the closing figures from the June 2026 quarterly and treats the announced value as signing-date only. D2 is applied by not using the September 2025 total debt as an input. D3 is resolved by arithmetic here: the maturity table total 2,785,200 equals total debt outstanding 2,780,917 plus other borrowings 4,283 (C10), although the filing does not state that bridge. D4 is refined above. D5 is resolved in part: segment capital expenditures of 318,579 for six months equal the cash purchase of property, plant and equipment (page:9, page:34), while growth capital expenditure is a different company measure that includes accrual and non-cash items; the segment allocation of the accrual difference is not disclosed, so the power segment figures 118,012 and 134,371 are not bridged (C11). D6 is applied by labelling the segment basis in every table. Its gaps G1 and G2 (no credit agreement, no 2026 covenant levels) restrict the covenant table above; G6 (preliminary purchase accounting) and G7 (no three-segment annual recast) restrict the acquisition and segment content; G5 (no filing after the June 2026 quarter) fixes the latest balance sheet date; G11 (management ratios appear only in releases) is why the 3.5x, 3.6x and 3.2x are shown as attributed claims. - C5. Unadjusted EBITDA and add-backs. LTM June 2026: net income 80,572 + interest 204,193 + tax (31,884 + 23,853 - 23,969 = 31,768) + D&A (276,185 + 147,331 - 136,664 = 286,852) = 603,385; add-backs: loss on extinguishment 36,512; disposal of business 33,349; sales tax reserve 27,968; loss on sale of assets 28,217 + 4,220 - 15,817 = 16,620; equity compensation 24,529 + 14,529 - 13,269 = 25,789; transaction expenses 4,102 + 11,615 - 1,786 = 13,931; severance 2,497 + 72 - 376 = 2,193; impairment 6,344; total 162,706; 603,385 + 162,706 = 766,091 (equal to C1). ### Business and transaction view

Kodiak's credit story is a contract compression operator with fixed-fee, multi-year contracts, high fleet utilisation and customers described as large upstream and midstream companies, that is in the middle of a strategic widening into distributed power. On the evidence, the compression core is stable and gaining visibility: remaining performance obligations rose sharply in the second quarter of 2026 and utilisation was 98.2%. The power build is the new variable. The acquisition closed on April 1, 2026, the acquired business has produced one quarter of results, only one customer lease is disclosed in detail, and purchase commitments rose to $2.5 billion. The financial handoff shows an equity offering, a refinanced notes stack and a largely undrawn ABL alongside this growth, which supports near-term liquidity but moves the credit from a steady-state contract business toward a capital-intensive build in which the pace of customer contracting, not demand commentary, matters. Ownership is public: the former sponsor affiliate exited in 2025, so no sponsor is documented as supporting or controlling the credit. Documented capital allocation shows both shareholder distributions and equity issuance; no priming, drop-down, non-pro-rata exchange or collateral release is documented in the pack. Governance evidence is limited to filing summaries because the proxy statement and executed financing documents are not supplied.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The transaction that matters most is the acquisition of Distributed Power Solutions, LLC, a provider of turnkey distributed and behind-the-meter power generation, by Kodiak Gas Services, LLC. The type is an acquisition of 100% of the equity interests for cash and registrant shares. Signing was on February 5, 2026 at a value of approximately $675.0 million at signing, comprising $575.0 million of cash and 2,401,278 shares valued at approximately $100.0 million on a $41.64 five-day average price, with a $37.1 million termination fee payable by the registrant in certain circumstances (10-K pages 25 and 139). Closing was April 1, 2026 on cash of $587.3 million, adjusted for additional power generation assets bought before closing, indebtedness and working capital, and 2.4 million shares with an estimated fair value of $139.0 million at the $57.90 closing price, so the fair value of consideration transferred was 726,354 thousand USD (10-Q 2026-06-30 pages 12 and 13; 10-Q 2026-03-31 page 24). The sellers are not named in the acquisition note; the registration rights agreement entered at closing names Mustang PRS, LLC and Louisiana Machinery Company, L.L.C. as holders of the registrant shares issued in the transaction (10-Q 2026-03-31 page 24); the pack does not otherwise name the sellers. The purchase price allocation is preliminary and recognises goodwill of 344,782 thousand USD, all in the Power Infrastructure reporting unit (10-Q 2026-06-30 pages 13 and 19). The pack contains no bridge between the signing and closing values, so the difference is logged as a conflict below and not reconciled. The stated rationale, which is management language, is to expand beyond contract compression into distributed power generation and enhance revenue growth through scale and complementary services (10-Q 2026-06-30 page 12). Liquidity effect and use of proceeds: the notes and equity transactions that followed are described below; the pack does not state which source funded which part of the cash consideration, and the financial handoff shows cash paid net of cash acquired of 575,965 thousand USD in the first half of 2026. The status is complete, with the allocation open for up to one year from closing.

New debt in the period. On March 20, 2026 Kodiak Services issued $1.0 billion of 5.875% senior unsecured notes due 2031, with fees of $14.3 million, and used a portion of the net proceeds to redeem all $750.0 million of its 7.25% notes due 2029 at 103.625 percent, through a defeasance on March 30, 2026 that required a $785.5 million cash outlay and produced a loss on extinguishment of 36,512 thousand USD (10-Q 2026-06-30 pages 21 to 23). The 2029 notes were redeemed April 10, 2026. On April 2, 2026 Kodiak and Kodiak Services signed the Fifth Amendment to the ABL credit agreement, which modifies the leverage ratio calculation by allowing net proceeds of the 2031 notes to be deducted from total indebtedness, in addition to the $50.0 million cash netting cap, through June 30, 2026 (page 21). In the prior year, on September 5, 2025 Kodiak Services issued $600.0 million each of 6.50% notes due 2033 and 6.75% notes due 2035, with add-ons of $170.0 million and $30.0 million on September 22, 2025, using the proceeds to repay part of the ABL, and a Fourth Amendment to the ABL reduced commitments to $2.0 billion and extended maturity to September 2030 (10-Q 2026-06-30 page 23; 10-K page 72), the amendment date not being stated in the text read. The equity side: an underwritten offering of 10.6 million shares at $71.00, with a further 1.6 million shares under the option, closed May 15, 2026 for net proceeds of approximately $836.1 million (10-Q 2026-06-30 page 26). The pack does not state a use of proceeds for that offering, and the financial handoff shows ABL drawings fell in the quarter; the link is an inference, not a documented fact. After quarter end Kodiak exercised options to buy about 43,000 horsepower of leased compression equipment for about $32.8 million in July 2026 and declared a $0.49 per share dividend on August 5, 2026 (10-Q 2026-06-30 pages 29 and 35). The financial handoff carries the resulting leverage, liquidity and maturity figures: total debt to LTM adjusted EBITDA of 3.63x, liquidity of 1,742.0 US$m, and purchase commitments of $2.5 billion. Parties, status and amounts above are Documentary Facts; the stated rationales are Management Language; the possible link between the equity offering and ABL repayment is Analyst Interpretation.

No rating event is in the pack. No event dated after the August 6, 2026 release appears.
### Revenue visibility: remaining performance obligations

Compression segment remaining performance obligations, USD thousands, with the Contract Services label used before the June 2026 rename (10-K page:116-117; 10-Q 2026-03-31 page:10; 10-Q 2026-06-30 page:17):
| Date | 2026 (or remainder) | 2027 | 2028 | 2029 | 2030 | Thereafter | Total |

The share of the total falling in 2028 or later is 15.9% at December 31, 2025, 21.4% at March 31, 2026 and 49.9% at June 30, 2026 (Calculation A1). The total rose by 1,010,319 thousand USD in the second quarter, and the pack gives no explanation of the increase; the mix of renewals, new contracts and the measurement basis cannot be assessed. The power business has no equivalent disclosure because lease revenue under lease accounting is excluded from the performance obligation disclosure (10-Q 2026-06-30 page:17).
### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: fixed monthly fees with primary terms of one to seven years (10-K page:16), 9.0% of revenue-generating horsepower on month-to-month terms, and performance obligations of 2,643,245 thousand USD at June 30, 2026 against LTM compression revenue of 1,220,890 thousand USD (Calculation A2). Mechanic: take-or-pay-style fees convert fleet utilisation into near-term revenue regardless of volumes, and the rise in obligations extends the contracted period. Implication: supports near-term revenue visibility and debt service; the step up is unexplained, and the tail beyond 2027 was thin until the second quarter. Counter: the shorter-term tail and month-to-month contracts are the exposure if basin activity weakens.

2. Margin and cash-flow risk (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: Compression adjusted gross margin of 70.0% in the second quarter against Other Services at 11.3%, below 15.9% in the first quarter of 2026 and 24.5% a year earlier (release 2026-08-06 page:6), with receivables and working capital absorbing cash in the first half (financial handoff, cash flow quality). Mechanic: the high-margin compression stream carries the credit; Other Services margin erosion and working capital drag reduce cash conversion. Implication: credit metrics on adjusted EBITDA overstate cash earnings in 2026; the financial handoff shows operating cash flow at 62.5% of LTM adjusted EBITDA.

3. Concentration risk (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: 82.8% of compression assets in the Permian Basin and Eagle Ford (10-K page:13), four largest customers about 32% of revenue and one customer 14%, and a limited number of suppliers. Mechanic: basin activity, a single large customer's decisions and equipment lead times drive utilisation and growth timing. Implication: loss of the largest customer or a supplier disruption would have a disproportionate effect on utilisation and growth timing; no peer comparison is made.

4. Transformation and execution risk in power (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: one disclosed lease with initial term to April 1, 2028, revised power growth capital spending guidance, purchase commitments of $2.5 billion against $276.4 million at March 31, 2026 (10-Q 2026-03-31 page:34), and a one gigawatt turbine order (release 2026-08-06 page:2). Mechanic: equipment is bought before multi-year contracts are shown, so cash is committed ahead of revenue; power lease revenue was 8.4% of second quarter revenue (Calculation A3). Implication: liquidity of 1,742.0 US$m in the financial handoff must absorb a 12-month commitment of $587.9 million plus negative implied free cash flow; delays in contracting would raise leverage because EBITDA from the new assets lags the financing. Counter: management states customer discussions are advanced, a Management Language claim that is not backed by executed contracts in the pack.

5. Sponsor alignment (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: the sponsor affiliate holding fell to zero by December 2, 2025 with no proceeds to Kodiak. Mechanic: with no sponsor, distributions and acquisitions are decided by a public-company board under the covenant package; ABL-funded dividends require $100,000,000 pro forma availability. Implication: no sponsor is documented as available to provide support, and equity issuance at market is the demonstrated support route; monitoring should track distributions against free cash flow, which in 2025 were 263,525 thousand USD against company free cash flow of 229,581 thousand USD (Calculation A4).

6. Key uncertainties (Analyst Interpretation). Preliminary purchase accounting; an unquantified sanctions-related matter; unexplained allowance write-offs; and no executed financing documents. Each is a gap below.
### Conflicts

The filings state the causes (cash adjustments for additional assets, indebtedness and working capital; a closing price of $57.90 against a $41.64 signing average) but do not quantify each; this handoff cites each at its own date |

| Sponsor holdings | CP-0 gap G9 and entity row stated current holdings were not stated | 10-K page:25 and page:63 state ownership fell to zero by December 2, 2025 | Corrected below |
### Corrections to earlier handoffs

The source-readiness handoff stated, in its entity roles table and in its gap on ownership, that the former sponsor affiliate's current ownership was not stated. The annual report does state it: ownership reduced from approximately 43.1% at the start of 2025 to zero by December 2, 2025 (10-K page:25, page:63). That correction stands in this handoff; the earlier handoff cannot be edited. What remains a gap is a beneficial ownership table for current holders and the status of the Stockholders' Agreement and Registration Rights Agreement. The financial-base handoff stated that dividends require pro forma ABL availability of at least $100,000,000; the filing states that condition for dividends funded with ABL borrowings (10-Q 2026-06-30 page:48), so the earlier statement is broader than the source. The rest of the financial-base handoff is consistent with the sources read here.

## Calculations

- A2. Coverage of LTM compression revenue by obligations: LTM revenue 1,181,270 (FY2025 Contract Services) + 622,110 (H1 2026) - 582,490 (H1 2025) = 1,220,890 thousand USD; 2,643,245 / 1,220,890 = 2.17 times. The FY2025 line is the earlier Contract Services label, which the June 2026 filing says was renamed; whether definitions are identical is stated only as a rename (10-Q 2026-06-30 page:33).

- A3. Power share of revenue: second quarter 32,891 / 391,120 = 8.4%; first half 32,891 / 736,879 = 4.5%. Disclosed power lease rental revenue to the end of the initial term: 13.7 + 27.4 + 6.9 = 48.0 million USD.

- A4. Distributions against free cash flow, 2025: dividends 159,557 + repurchases 103,968 = 263,525 thousand USD; company free cash flow 229,581; excess 33,944. Company free cash flow is a non-GAAP measure defined before dividends (financial base handoff).

- A6. Second-quarter allowance write-offs: first-half write-offs 14,578 less first-quarter write-offs 33 = 14,545; allowance roll: 14,167 + second-quarter provision (2,348 - 1,169 = 1,179) - 14,545 = 801, equal to the printed balance.

- A5. Consideration mix at closing: shares 139,034 / 726,354 = 19.1% of the fair value of consideration; the remainder is cash and adjustments. Cash 587.3 million is quoted rounded in the filing, so no exact split is claimed.

Fundamental credit synthesis of Kodiak Gas Services, Inc. (KGS), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, reporting currency USD, latest balance sheet date June 30, 2026. It uses only the settled financial-base and business-context handoffs. Scope is business risk, financial risk, liquidity and the gaps that limit them, with no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on, through the upstream handoffs
No source page was read again for this module; every fact below comes from the handoffs listed next, which cite these sources.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Kodiak is a contract compression credit with contracted revenue and liquidity of USD 1,742.0 million, but leverage of 3.63x is no longer falling quickly because power growth spending outruns cash flow; funding and execution of that build decide the outcome. | Medium | Covenant definitions, executed financing documents and power customer contracts are not supplied, so covenant headroom and power revenue visibility cannot be tested. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Compression revenue is contracted: remaining performance obligations were USD 2,643.2 million at June 2026 and fleet utilisation was 98.2%. | Supports near-term debt service; the sharp rise in obligations is not explained in the filings. | Medium |

| Total debt was 3.63x LTM adjusted EBITDA at June 2026, against 4.31x at FY2024 and 3.66x at FY2025, after an equity raise. | Leverage tolerance improved, but indicative year-end leverage on guidance stays near current levels. | Medium |

| Liquidity of USD 1,742.0 million exceeds twelve-month purchase commitments of USD 587.9 million, but guidance implies negative 2026 free cash flow. | Near-term liquidity is adequate; any shortfall falls on the ABL, which matures in 2030. | Medium |
| Add-backs were 21.2% of LTM adjusted EBITDA and operating cash flow was 62.5% of it. | Cash earnings are weaker than adjusted metrics suggest. | High |

| The power build rests on one disclosed lease running to April 1, 2028 and on covenant terms that are not supplied. | Funding ahead of contract evidence raises refinancing and covenant-monitoring needs. | Medium |
### Credit view

Kodiak Gas Services is a moderately leveraged contract compression credit whose strength is contracted, high-margin revenue and ample liquidity, and whose main exposure is a power build financed ahead of contracts. Compression remaining performance obligations of USD 2,643.2 million, utilisation of 98.2% and total debt of 3.63x LTM adjusted EBITDA after an equity raise of USD 836.1 million support the credit, with liquidity of USD 1,742.0 million and no scheduled debt maturity of size before 2030. The weakest point is that growth spending outruns cash generation: purchase commitments are USD 2.5 billion, guidance implies negative 2026 free cash flow, and only one power lease is disclosed. Delivery of power contracts against that spending, and covenant headroom that cannot be recomputed here, decide the outcome.
| Driver | Assessment | Category | Confidence |
| Business risk | Moderate: strong contracted compression base, new risk concentrated in power | Analyst Interpretation | Medium |
| Financial risk | Moderate: leverage lower than FY2024 and FY2025, cash conversion weaker | Analyst Interpretation | Medium |
| Liquidity | Adequate through the next twelve months | Documentary Fact for the inputs; Analyst Interpretation for the view | Medium |
| Control and alignment | No sponsor; public-company governance and documented distributions | Documentary Fact | Medium |
| Information quality | Limited by missing executed documents and contracts | Insufficient Information | Not assessable |
### Thesis

Kodiak's cash-generative, contracted compression fleet and equity-supported balance sheet carry the credit through a power build whose repayment capacity is not yet evidenced by contracts (Analyst Interpretation, resting on the contract, leverage and commitment rows below).
### Key findings

The first finding is revenue durability. Kodiak sells compression on fixed monthly fees under primary terms of one to seven years, with 9.0% of revenue-generating horsepower on month-to-month terms, and its compression remaining performance obligations were USD 2,643.2 million at June 30, 2026 against USD 1,632.9 million at March 31, 2026, with 49.9% falling in 2028 or later (Documentary Fact, from the business-context handoff). The mechanism is that fixed fees turn 98.2% utilisation into revenue largely independent of volume, so contracted obligations of 2.17 times LTM compression revenue protect near-term coverage of debt service. The implication is stronger revenue visibility than the previous quarter showed, tempered because the filings do not explain the jump and the month-to-month tail would reprice quickly in a weak basin.

The second is financial risk and leverage. Total debt was USD 2,780.9 million, or 3.63x LTM adjusted EBITDA of USD 766.1 million, and net debt was 3.45x, against 4.31x total and 4.30x net at FY2024 and 3.66x total at FY2025 (Documentary Fact for inputs, Calculated in the financial-base handoff). The mechanism is that the May equity offering of USD 836.1 million arrived in the same period as the USD 576.0 million cash acquisition and a notes refinancing, so debt rose by USD 166.3 million since December 2025 while LTM adjusted EBITDA rose by USD 51.1 million. The implication for leverage tolerance is a stepped-down but not yet clearly falling ratio; the figure overstates leverage on a full-year perimeter because EBITDA from the acquired power business before April 1, 2026 is Not calculable, and management's covenant-basis ratio of 3.2x (Management Language) cannot be recomputed.

The third is funding and liquidity. Liquidity was USD 1,742.0 million (cash of USD 137.6 million and undrawn ABL capacity of USD 1,604.5 million, an upper bound because the borrowing base is not supplied), against purchase commitments of USD 2.5 billion, of which USD 587.9 million is expected within twelve months, up from USD 276.4 million at March 31, 2026. Revised 2026 guidance implies discretionary cash flow less growth and other capital spending of negative USD 235.0 million to negative USD 125.0 million, before dividends of about USD 49.5 million a quarter. The mechanism is that the spending is discretionary in timing but contractually committed once ordered, and the ABL, which matures September 5, 2030 and is secured on essentially all assets, is the funding backstop. The implication is that refinancing risk is low through 2029 but that net leverage, on the indicative sensitivity below, ends 2026 at about 3.27x to 3.52x, roughly where it is today, unless adjusted EBITDA beats guidance or equity is raised again (Analyst Interpretation).

The fourth is earnings and cash quality. Add-backs were USD 162.7 million, or 21.2% of LTM adjusted EBITDA, and unadjusted leverage on the same debt would be 4.61x; operating cash flow was 62.5% of LTM adjusted EBITDA against 83.9% in FY2025, as working capital used USD 154.6 million in the first half (Documentary Fact and Calculated). The mechanism is that equity compensation, a settled sales tax reserve and refinancing and acquisition costs sit outside adjusted EBITDA while the sales tax settlement and working capital absorbed cash. The implication is that adjusted-EBITDA coverage of 4.14x on cash interest paid is a ceiling on debt-service capacity, and monitoring should use operating cash flow.

The fifth is the power transition and ownership. The acquisition closed April 1, 2026 with fair value of consideration of USD 726.4 million (signing value was about USD 675.0 million, logged as a conflict, not reconciled), goodwill of USD 344.8 million on a preliminary allocation, one disclosed lease agreement whose initial term ends April 1, 2028, and no sponsor, since EQT affiliates sold their entire stake by December 2, 2025 (Documentary Fact). The mechanism is that equipment is bought before multi-year contracts are shown, and no sponsor is documented as available to cure a shortfall. The implication is that the next two to three quarters of power contract announcements and utilisation are the main evidence that will move the credit view either way.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Contracted revenue visibility is the first: fixed-fee compression contracts, 98.2% utilisation, performance obligations of USD 2,643.2 million, and customer cost pass-throughs for fuel and taxes (Documentary Fact; business-context handoff). Margin resilience is the second: compression adjusted gross margin was 70.0% in the second quarter and adjusted EBITDA margin was 55.4% (Documentary Fact; financial-base handoff), which cushions a revenue decline. Liquidity and maturity profile is the third: USD 1,742.0 million of liquidity, no scheduled maturity of size before the ABL in 2030, and notes of USD 1,000.0 million due 2031, USD 770.0 million due 2033 and USD 630.0 million due 2035 (Documentary Fact). Balance sheet response is the fourth: Kodiak issued USD 836.1 million of equity alongside a debt-financed acquisition (Documentary Fact), which is documented equity support. Secured debt is the fifth: only the USD 380.9 million drawn on the ABL is secured, equal to 0.50x LTM adjusted EBITDA on this analysis (Analyst Interpretation, indicative only because the covenant definition of senior secured debt is not supplied).

Weaknesses. Growth spending against cash flow is the first: commitments of USD 2.5 billion and guidance that implies negative free cash flow in 2026 (Analyst Interpretation on Documentary Fact inputs). Earnings quality is the second: add-backs of 21.2% of LTM adjusted EBITDA and weaker cash conversion of 62.5% (Documentary Fact and Calculated). Concentration is the third: 82.8% of compression assets in the Permian Basin and Eagle Ford, four customers at about 32% of revenue and one at 14%, and dependence on a limited number of suppliers (Documentary Fact). Power visibility is the fourth: one disclosed lease agreement, so most power revenue is Not disclosed in contract terms, and a power fleet utilisation of 89.6% in its first quarter (Documentary Fact; the conclusion that visibility is thin is Analyst Interpretation). Covenant opacity is the fifth: the maximum Leverage Ratio of 5.25 to 1.00 printed in the annual report is on a defined basis not supplied, and the amended calculation applied only through June 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact; headroom is Insufficient Information). Unquantified contingencies are the sixth: a sanctions-related payments matter with no estimated penalty and a sales tax liability disclosed on two bases (Documentary Fact; exposure is Insufficient Information, not an adverse conclusion).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |
| Power execution and contracting | Equipment ordered ahead of signed multi-year leases; EBITDA lags spending | Leverage rises if contracting is slow; liquidity absorbs the gap | Material |

| Funding of capital commitments | Commitments of USD 2.5 billion and negative implied free cash flow in 2026 | Dependence on the ABL (matures 2030) and further equity; refinancing need beyond 2029 | Material |
| Cash conversion and earnings quality | Add-backs of 21.2% and operating cash flow at 62.5% of adjusted EBITDA | Debt service relies on adjusted earnings that exceed cash earnings | Material |

| Covenant headroom not testable | Covenant EBITDA and debt definitions, and the amended terms, not supplied | A covenant breach cannot be ruled in or out; monitoring posture depends on later disclosure | Material |
| Concentration (basin, customer, supplier) | 82.8% Permian and Eagle Ford; four customers 32%; limited suppliers | Utilisation and growth timing are exposed to single decisions | Material |
| Acquisition accounting and integration | Preliminary allocation; goodwill of USD 344.8 million | Impairment or changed asset values could alter reported leverage and equity | Minor |
| Sanctions-related payments matter | Self-reported to US authorities; penalty not estimated | Potential cash cost and compliance changes, size unknown; not an adverse conclusion | Minor |

| Structural subordination and recovery mechanics | The ABL is secured on essentially all assets, the notes are unsecured, guarantor identities are not supplied | Claims on collateral rank ahead of the unsecured notes; no recovery conclusion is drawn | Material |
### Monitoring posture

Four items should be tracked each quarter, in this order: free cash flow against the USD 587.9 million of twelve-month commitments and the ABL balance; announcements of signed power leases and power utilisation against the 89.6% first-quarter level; the covenant leverage ratio and any amended terms, once the credit agreement is supplied; and conversion of performance obligations, to see whether the second-quarter jump reflects durable new contracts.
## Calculations
All inputs come from the upstream handoffs; amounts in USD thousands unless stated.

- D1. Debt and EBITDA change since December 2025: total debt 2,780,917 - 2,614,647 = 166,270; LTM adjusted EBITDA 766,091 - 715,033 (FY2025) = 51,058. Cash acquisition cost 575,965 (net of cash acquired). Contracted obligations to LTM compression revenue: 2,643,245 / 1,220,890 = 2.17 times (financial base and business context handoffs).

- D2. Indicative year-end 2026 net leverage on management guidance (Analyst Interpretation, not a forecast). Full-year guidance: discretionary cash flow 570,000 to 600,000; growth and other capital spending 725,000 to 805,000; adjusted EBITDA 830,000 to 860,000. First half actuals: discretionary cash flow 289,756; growth and other capital spending 134,357 + 152,356 + 61,167 = 347,880. Implied second half: best case 600,000 - 289,756 = 310,244 of discretionary cash flow against 725,000 - 347,880 = 377,120 of spending, a shortfall of 66,876; worst case 570,000 - 289,756 = 280,244 against 805,000 - 347,880 = 457,120, a shortfall of 176,876. Add dividends of two quarters at 49,541 = 99,082 (per share dividend of USD 0.49 on 101,104,031 shares, constant). Net debt need: 165,958 (best) and 275,958 (worst). Net debt at June 30, 2026 is 2,643,364, so year-end net debt is 2,809,322 (best) and 2,919,322 (worst). Net leverage: best 2,809,322 / 860,000 = 3.27x; worst 2,919,322 / 830,000 = 3.52x. Gross total debt equivalents, holding cash constant: (2,780,917 + 165,958) / 860,000 = 3.43x and (2,780,917 + 275,958) / 830,000 = 3.68x. The inputs mix company non-GAAP definitions with guidance; asset sale proceeds, working capital, further equity and interest on additional borrowings are not modelled.
- D3. Liquidity cover of twelve-month commitments: 587,900 / 1,742,036 = 33.7% of June 2026 liquidity (financial base handoff); liquidity less commitments 1,742,036 - 587,900 = 1,154,136.
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |

| Credit agreement, Fifth Amendment and indentures not supplied; covenant definitions, amended terms, guarantors and restricted subsidiaries unknown | Covenant headroom, legal capacity for distributions and debt, and structural claims cannot be assessed | Covenants, structure, monitoring | Material | Add executed documents |

| Power customer contracts and portfolio beyond one disclosed lease not disclosed | Revenue visibility of the new segment cannot be tested | Business risk, leverage trajectory | Material | Add contract summaries or later disclosures |

| Pro forma EBITDA for the acquired power business before April 1, 2026 is Not calculable | LTM leverage overstates leverage on a full-year perimeter; direction and size unknown | Leverage | Material | Obtain acquired-business earnings |
| ABL borrowing base not supplied | Undrawn capacity is an upper bound | Liquidity | Minor | Add borrowing base disclosure |

| Use of the equity offering proceeds not stated; reason for the jump in performance obligations and for allowance write-offs not disclosed | The sources of funding and the quality of the new contract base are not traceable | Funding, revenue visibility | Minor | Add offering documents and management explanation |
| No filing for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | Latest balance sheet is June 30, 2026; the cutoff is 2026-11-05 | All | Material | Add any later periodic filing dated on or before the cutoff |
| No ratings, market data or peer data; context fields blank | No market-implied view and no relative metrics are produced; not an adverse conclusion | Market views | Minor | Supply if wanted |
| Sanctions-related matter unquantified; purchase accounting preliminary; sales tax shown on two bases | Contingent and measurement uncertainty | Contingencies | Minor | Monitor |

| Beneficial ownership table, proxy statement and status of stockholder agreements with the former sponsor affiliate not supplied | Governance and control rights cannot be confirmed as ended | Control and alignment | Minor | Add the proxy statement |
## Next module

Proceed to CP-5, which should trace each material claim above to the financial-base and business-context handoffs: the leverage, liquidity, add-back and cash conversion figures and calculations C1 to C11, the commitments and guidance inputs to calculation D2, and the fact rows on contracts, sponsor exit and capital allocation. It should treat calculation D2 as Analyst Interpretation, the management covenant ratio and growth claims as Management Language, and the covenant, power contract and pro forma EBITDA items as open gaps.

## Calculations
Independent recomputation from the cited source figures (USD thousands unless stated). Each reproduces the upstream result.

- R3. Carrying-value basis (new check, canon basis): long-term debt net of issuance cost 2,720,989 plus other borrowings 4,283 = 2,725,272 (printed as total long-term debt and other borrowings, S4 page:20). 2,725,272 / 766,091 = 3.56x; (2,725,272 - 137,553) / 766,091 = 3.38x. Gross delta between principal total debt outstanding and the net carrying value: 2,780,917 - 2,720,989 = 59,928, equal to unamortized debt issuance cost 63,817 less unamortized premium 3,889. FY2025 on the same basis: (2,555,250 + 395) / 715,033 = 3.57x.

- R7. Guidance range: 570,000 - 805,000 = (235,000); 600,000 - 725,000 = (125,000). Year-end sensitivity: best (2,643,364 + 165,958) / 860,000 = 3.27x; worst (2,643,364 + 275,958) / 830,000 = 3.52x, with the shortfalls 66,876 and 176,876 plus dividends 99,082 as stated in the synthesis.
- R8. Distributions: 159,557 + 103,968 = 263,525; less company free cash flow 229,581 = 33,944.

- R9. Cross-module numeric match: every figure in the synthesis prose matches a figure or calculation in the financial-base or business-context handoffs, except the synthesis's own calculations and the three capital-spending inputs from S4 page:58 (issue I-10).
## Gaps

The evidence gaps limiting this review are listed in the gaps ledger above (TG1 to TG7). Two limits apply to the review itself. First, the review tested the figures and quotations that the handoffs cite for their material claims (53 strings checked at their cited pages), not every figure in every table, so a non-material slip outside that set could remain. Second, no extraction fidelity review of the source text against the original filings was performed; the sources were treated as the retained text. Neither limit changes the findings above, but both bound the confidence in the review.
